summary: Iteration 4 tested the Lugg/Porter features. Backend: 75/75 pytest pass (67 existing + 8 new in test_lugg_porter_features.py). These cover coupons (invalid code, wrong category, LUGG10 cap of ₹200), tip limits and tip going 100% to the partner, helpers minimum and labour scaling, the 3-stop limit, OTP hidden from the partner in list/detail/accept, rating rules, skipped status steps rejected, tips in earnings, cancellation refunds, and category/slot/stops saved on the order. Frontend (375x667 web preview): all 6 category cards show, and the step-1 subtitle shows the category name ('Step 1 of 3 · Junk removal'). Add a stop stops at 3, remove works, and all 7 time slots show and can be selected. Vehicle choice changes the price (₹350 to ₹550 base). Helpers stepper: 0 helpers removes labour and loading for shift_only; pack_and_shift stays at a minimum of 1; 2 helpers doubles labour. Hours stepper bills 1 helper × 1.5 hr × ₹200 = ₹300. Coupons: invalid code and MOVE200 on junk removal both show a message, and FIRST50 and LUGG10 add a discount line before GST. Remove button works. ₹100 tip adds an invoice-tip row and raises Total payable and partner payout by ₹100, while invoice-total excludes the tip. Junk removal adds the Eco-disposal fee; intercity at 350 km adds the toll line. Customer sees the OTP card (DEMO0003 = 1236). Partner sees no OTP card; a wrong OTP shows the 400 toast and the correct OTP moves the order to picked up → in transit → delivered. Rating card submits once, then shows read-only. Partner home shows 4.0★ and 'Includes ₹100.00 in tips'. Cancelling after a partner is assigned shows 'Refund of ₹835.00 ... (₹100 cancellation fee ...)'. No deprecated Expo packages found.

minor.issue: Labour label grammar: 'Labour (2 helper × 2.5 hr × ₹350)' should say 'helpers' for more than 1
The toll/permit charge is added to any category when distance > 100 km, not only intercity. This may be intended; please confirm.

ui_bugs.issue: A single tap cancels right away. There is no confirmation dialog and no warning that a ₹100 fee applies once a partner is assigned, so an accidental tap costs the user money.
